precautions: Scout fields weekly; start interventions early when symptoms are first seen.
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day; keep foliage as dry as possible.
Sanitize tools and remove heavily infected plant debris from the field.
Balance NPK; excess nitrogen encourages soft, disease-prone growth.
cultural_controls: Ensure adequate spacing and airflow; prune lower leaves to reduce humidity.
Rotate crops (2–3 years) and avoid planting on infected residues.
organic_options: Horticultural oil or neem oil for surface suppression (apply in the cool hours).
Potassium bicarbonate or bicarbonate+oil mixes can knock back light infections.
Copper-based protectants (use sparingly to avoid copper buildup).
chemical_options: Rotate different FRAC modes of action to prevent resistance.
Always follow local regulations and product labels for crops and pre-harvest intervals.
Generic.note: Local labels and permitted actives vary by region; verify with your state agriculture department/extension.

Healthy.summary: Leaf looks mostly healthy. Keep monitoring.
precautions: Continue weekly scouting; remove any new infected leaves promptly.
Irrigate at the base and avoid wetting foliage, especially overnight.
cultural_controls: Maintain balanced fertilization and good airflow.
Mulch to reduce soil splash and weed hosts.
organic_options: No treatment needed; you may use preventive protectants during wet/humid spells (sulfur or copper as label allows).
chemical_options: Preventive sprays usually not necessary; if disease pressure historically high, consider a protectant before forecasted humidity/rain.
Healthy.note: Overuse of fungicides without confirmed disease can drive resistance and wastes money.

Leaf Rust.summary: Rust typically shows as orange-brown powdery pustules on leaves.
precautions: Destroy volunteer/alternate hosts and crop residues that harbor rust.
Avoid excessive late nitrogen which drives lush, susceptible growth.
cultural_controls: Use resistant varieties; sow at recommended dates (avoid very late sowing).
Ensure airflow; do not overcrowd plants.
organic_options: Sulfur (wettable sulfur/dust) applied early can suppress rust development.
Copper-based protectants provide broad surface protection (observe labels).
chemical_options: Multi-site protectants (FRAC M03/M01) e.g., mancozeb, copper oxychloride.
Rotate FRAC groups and mix a protectant with a single-site active to slow resistance.
Leaf Rust.note: Follow label crop lists and PHIs. Some actives may be restricted or phased out in certain countries.

Leaf Blight.summary: Leaf blight (often Alternaria/Helminthosporium) causes tan/brown lesions that may coalesce.
precautions: Irrigate early in the day to reduce leaf wetness; avoid overhead irrigation if possible.
Remove and destroy infected residues; avoid working in fields when foliage is wet.
cultural_controls: Wider spacing and pruning to reduce humidity and improve airflow.
2–3 year rotation away from susceptible hosts; use certified, disease-free seed.
organic_options: Copper-based protectants for general suppression (watch total seasonal copper).
Bicarbonate + oil mixes can help on very early infections.
chemical_options: Protectants: mancozeb (FRAC M03), chlorothalonil* (FRAC M05)*, copper oxychloride (FRAC M01).
Rotate modes of action and tank-mix with a multi-site where allowed.
Leaf Blight.note: Chlorothalonil is restricted in some regions; verify legality. Always observe label rates and PHIs.

Powdery Mildew.summary: Powdery white/gray growth on upper leaf surfaces; thrives in dry days + humid nights.
precautions: Avoid excess nitrogen; increase airflow by pruning or wider spacing.
Do not overhead irrigate late evening; reduce humidity around canopy.
cultural_controls: Remove the most infected leaves early to lower inoculum.
organic_options: Potassium bicarbonate sprays; horticultural oils (paraffinic/neem) on light infections.
chemical_options: Rotate FRAC groups; avoid back-to-back sprays of the same MOA.
Powdery Mildew.note: Do not spray sulfur within ~2 weeks of oil applications; risk of phytotoxicity in high heat.
